WHY IT EXISTS, in one sentence: rulings were STORED perfectly and REACHABLE only by
someone who already suspected they existed. #54 ruled the token unit; the ruling sits in
#80 re-derived it from scratch 26 sessions later and nearly filed it as a discovery, and
#81 started down the same path before Dave named the circling. Searching the archive for
the topic returns THIS WEEK'S BANNERS, because retrieval ranks recency above rulings.
SO THE TRIGGER IS NOT A SEARCH. It is the WORK ITSELF: `git diff --name-only` at build and
wrap. Touch a governed file, and the ruling that governs it is printed at you whether or
not you thought to ask. That is the entire mechanism, and it is deliberately not clever.
[WARN] THIS FILE IS A POINTER INDEX, NEVER A SECOND COPY OF CANON. `says` is a one-line
reminder whose job is to make you go and read `evidence`. If a ruling's substance ever
lives HERE, the index has become an eleventh place to store it and the defect is back.
ADDING ONE: an entry is cheap and a missing entry is what this file exists to prevent.
Add a ruling when Dave rules something that governs code or canon someone will later touch
without remembering. `governs` accepts repo-relative paths and bare symbol names.

Therefore the coloured-text rung MUST be per-mode - this is WHY it is a separate rung and not an edit to the mode-invariant s122-D2 fills.

The tool reported the clip; nothing chased what the clip IMPLIED, and hue lock was the whole premise. v2 added a hard guard clamping chroma at the gamut boundary ALONG the locked hue - driven at 2.6x the gamut ceiling, hue held to +0.087 deg.
findings.hue-can-be-locked-in-one-space-only: green-light carries an OKLCH hue drift of -4.53 deg (#137F3C sits at OKLCH hue 150.06 vs locked 154.5908) while its HSB drift is -0.16 deg. v2's alarm keys to the DRIVING model (HSB) so it stayed silent. This is a PROPERTY, not a defect: HSB is not perceptually uniform, so moving saturation/brightness in HSB always shifts OKLCH hue. Hue can be locked in one space or the other, NOT BOTH. Same shape as the mode-invariance impossibility. Dave accepted it as tuned.
